title: Why the Pacific Islands Forum Should Watch Taiwan’s East Coast
gist: Ahead of the 55th Pacific Islands Forum in Palau, member states failed to reach consensus on criticizing China's submarine-based ballistic missile testing in the Pacific, even as normalization of Chinese naval activity east of Taiwan creates an under-recognized maritime pressure point bordering forum members' exclusive economic zones.

themes.theme: PIF split over China criticism and Taiwan's east coast as an overlooked flashpoint

insights.claim: Ahead of the 55th Pacific Islands Forum, scheduled for August 30 to September 4 in Palau, Pacific Island leaders failed to reach consensus on a joint statement criticizing China's submarine-based ballistic missile testing in the Pacific.
insights.speaker: Domingo I-Kwei Yang
insights.so_what: A failure to reach consensus signals divergent threat perceptions among Pacific states toward China, a fracture line relevant to assessing the durability of any unified Pacific pushback on Chinese military activity.
insights.quote: Pacific Island leaders failed to reach consensus on a joint statement criticizing China’s submarine-based ballistic missile testing in the Pacific.
insights.locator: Pacific Island leaders failed to reach

insights.claim: The split within the Pacific Islands Forum reflects intensifying great-power competition and divergent threat perceptions between external powers and Pacific governments themselves.
insights.speaker: Domingo I-Kwei Yang
insights.so_what: Divergence between external powers' framing and Pacific governments' own threat assessments means outside actors (US, Australia) may struggle to marshal unified Pacific opposition to Chinese activity.
insights.quote: The split reflects intensifying great-power competition and divergent threat perceptions between external powers and Pacific governments.

insights.claim: The growing normalization of Chinese naval and coast guard activity in the waters east of Taiwan is a less visible source of pressure on Pacific Island states that the Pacific Islands Forum has not yet connected to its own maritime interests.
insights.speaker: Domingo I-Kwei Yang
insights.so_what: This maritime gateway feeds directly into Pacific states' exclusive economic zones, meaning escalation east of Taiwan carries direct spillover risk for Pacific Island fisheries, shipping lanes, and EEZ sovereignty that the PIF has not yet priced into its threat assessment.
insights.quote: the growing normalization of Chinese naval and coast guard activity in the waters east of Taiwan, a development the PIF has yet to fully connect to its own maritime interests.
insights.locator: another less visible source of pressure

insights.claim: The maritime gateway east of Taiwan leads directly into the exclusive economic zones that the Pacific Islands Forum seeks to protect, and deserves greater attention from Pacific Island states.
insights.speaker: Domingo I-Kwei Yang
insights.so_what: Watch for whether the PIF's August 30-September 4 Palau summit expands its China-related agenda beyond missile testing to include naval activity east of Taiwan, which would signal a broadening of Pacific security concerns tied to Taiwan Strait tensions.
insights.quote: This maritime gateway east of Taiwan leads directly into the exclusive economic zones that the forum seeks to protect and deserves greater attention from Pacific Island states.
insights.locator: This maritime gateway east of Taiwan
